summary: Block 13. (1) Corrected the §8 application claim, which had silently switched recursions. With `scale := t` the generic rule is t_n = min(t_{n-1}/2, 1/(n+2)) - the next budget depends on the previous BUDGET, not on the previous epsilon - and it says nothing about the ordering of epsilon_n. Two legitimate routes are now stated separately: Route A (scale := t) gives monotone t -> 0 and hence epsilon_n < t_n -> 0 and sum rad_n < t_n -> 0, and needs one reindexing (dependent choice of phi with epsilon_{phi(n+1)} < epsilon_{phi(n)}/2, valid because convergence makes {m : epsilon_m < epsilon_n/2} cofinite and cofinite sets meet {m > n}) to make epsilon monotone, with every bound inherited since phi(n) >= n; Route B (scale := epsilon) gets monotone epsilon directly, with hsmall supplied by taking a witness at budget s/2 so epsilon < s, and then the per-index budget is t_n <= 1/(2(n+2)) -> 0, so radii converge too. One single-scale lemma suffices for both; no two-scale lemma is needed; selecting on epsilon without the s/2 step is the error the objection names. (2) Finished the Lemma 7.4(1)(2) source-to-paper comparison: item (2) is reproduced (codomain GraphSpace + agrees off diskHoles, with coreHoles <= diskHoles); item (1) is STRICTLY WEAKER in the Lean - MarkedDisk.Valid says only that a core disk meets L, and there is no injective bookkeeping x -> B_{n,x}, no 'precisely one', no containment in int Q - recorded as a statement-level difference and an open audit item, NOT a gap. Subsequence preservation: every clause is per-index, the only cross-index quantifier is 'eventually', so any strictly increasing phi with phi(n) >= n preserves items (1)-(3) and all fields. V3 remains staged, uncompiled; the running build was not touched.

My first block-6 check script applied the identity map instead of h and reported all identities false - a script bug, not a mathematical finding; corrected and re-run inside the same one-process budget.

`refine ⟨membership-proof, ?_⟩` for a `Finset.Nonempty` goal: Nonempty is `∃ a, a ∈ s`, so the witness must come first; the local run caught this at hasNbr_image and it also poisoned neighbour_family_push with sorryAx.

Restoring the paper's monotone eps_n from the Lean per-scale form: monotonicity cannot be obtained by replacing eps_n with min over k<=n, because shrinking eps changes pi^eps and hence the entire disk family and the agreement map; it would need the construction to be redone at the new scale. Recorded as the single loss of the interchange.

My earlier claim that monotonicity of eps_n cannot be restored: wrong, and now retracted with two explicit constructions. The error was conflating 'modifying a witness' (blocked, since shrinking eps changes pi^eps) with 'selecting among witnesses' (free, and carries all indexed data).

escalation.obstacle: (NC-1), restated precisely: at an accumulation point x of a specified five-cycle locus, with a = lim h_n/|h_n| and R the rotation acting on directions, the list S(R a) = {i : R a lies in the closed essential support of state i at x} has no common label, i.e. the intersection of the diagonals D_i over i in S(R a) is empty.
escalation.definitions: D_i = {i, i+2} in Z/5Z; state i at x = the set of directions whose palette is exactly D_i; closed essential support S_i = the closed set whose every neighbourhood meets state i in positive measure; S(u) = {i : u in S_i}.
